page: Amazon Web Services c6i.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features two Intel Xeon 8375C processors running on the x86_64 architecture, providing 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading at a clock rate of 3.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes 54 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1 data cache per core. Memory capacity stands at 256.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, offering a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector acceleration includes AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, while cryptographic operations are accelerated via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets.

The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, meaning persistent storage requires external network-attached volumes. Networking throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional parallel execution and vector compute capabilities. The c6i.32xlarge ranks in the top tier (top 10%) on the PassMark CPU overall score (86,621.37), CPU extended instructions test (106,808.88), CPU encryption test (111,188.79), and Geekbench ray tracing (91,666.0). Highly parallel benchmarks demonstrate strong performance (top 25%), including Geekbench multi-core (16,121.0), Geekbench software compilation using Clang (49,338.0), and stress-ng multi-core (123,842.49). Memory throughput is robust, showing 329.34 GB/sec read and 131.23 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256MB blocks.

In contrast, single-threaded processing ranks within the middle 50% average tier across Geekbench single-core (1,687.0), stress-ng single-core (1,893.1), and compression routines like gzip (28.6 GB/sec). Large language model text generation also falls into the average tier, producing 21.9 tokens/sec on 7B models and 2.93 tokens/sec on 70B models, though prompt processing speeds perform in the upper quartile due to AVX-512 vector support.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c6i.32xlarge maximizes resource density for CPU-bound tasks requiring wide parallelism and high network throughput without paying for unused GPU hardware or local NVMe drives. It is well-fitted for large-scale distributed computing, batch processing, static web serving (measuring 74.34 GB/sec), high-concurrency Clang compilation farms, and distributed in-memory databases such as Redis (processing 108.6 million SET operations/sec).
description: Amazon Web Services c6i.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and Intel Xeon 8375C processors. Configured with 64 physical cores, 128 dedicated vCPUs at 3.5 GHz, and 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory, it operates with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, lacks local disk storage, and features no hardware GPUs. CPU performance shines in vector mathematics and multi-threaded computation, achieving top-tier results in PassMark CPU tests, encryption, and Geekbench ray tracing. Memory bandwidth reaches 329.34 GB/sec on large block reads. While single-thread benchmarks align with median enterprise expectations, its high parallel throughput, static web serving output of 74.34 GB/sec, and 108.6 million Redis SET operations per second make it suited for distributed compilation, high-traffic web applications, and compute-heavy batch workloads.
